memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'A clay pot that the man touches must be broken, and any wooden article is to be rinsed with water.'" - Lev 15:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The same distinction we met earlier. Clay absorbs, so it breaks. Wood can be rinsed, so it stays.

The priest had to tell the difference — and so must we. Not everything in our lives that has been affected needs destroying. Some things need washing.

We often get this wrong in both directions. Some of us destroy what could have been cleaned. We walk away from a church over one disappointment, end a friendship after one hard conversation, abandon a calling because of one failure. We break what God intended us to rinse.

Others of us try to wash what needs breaking. We manage a habit that ought to end. We set limits on something that should be gone entirely. We keep negotiating with the porous clay pot.

Wisdom is knowing which is which — and that kind of wisdom is not something we generate. If any of you lacks wisdom, you should ask God, who gives generously to all without finding fault (Jas 1:5).

Before you break something, ask whether God is calling you to wash it. Before you keep managing something, ask whether God is calling you to break it. Then ask Him, honestly, and wait for the answer.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What in your life have you been managing that needs breaking?
2. What have you been ready to abandon that God may want restored?
3. Have you actually asked God for wisdom about it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, give me wisdom to tell the difference between what must be broken and what can be washed. Keep me from destroying what You want restored, and from clinging to what You want gone. Amen.
